mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.25% in a single month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of instances where FEDFUNDS increased by more than 0.25% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% in a month signals a weakening labor market, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as investors anticipate slower economic growth.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in more than 60% of instances where UNRATE rose by more than 0.5% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real GDP (GDPC1) for two consecutive quarters signals a recessionary environment, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings expectations are revised downwards.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 50% of instances where GDPC1 declined for two consecutive quarters.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% in a month signals strengthening economic activity, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as investor sentiment improves.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of instances where INDPRO increased by more than 1% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) for three consecutive months signals a strengthening housing market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as it indicates increased consumer confidence and economic activity.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in more than 40% of instances where HOUST increased for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is above 8% and payroll employment (PAYEMS) declines for two consecutive months, it signals a severe labor market weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as economic growth prospects dim.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE > 8% and PAYEMS declines for 2 months
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of instances where UNRATE was above 8% and PAYEMS declined for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is below 1% and the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) increases by more than 0.5% in a month, it signals inflationary pressure in a low-rate environment, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as real returns are eroded.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < 1% and CPIAUCSL increases > 0.5% in 1 month
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in more than 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS was below 1% and CPIAUCSL increased by more than 0.5% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: When real final sales of domestic product (RSAFS) decline for two consecutive months and the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) increases by more than 0.5% in the same period, it signals stagflation, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as economic growth slows and inflation rises.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS declines for 2 months and CPIAUCSL increases > 0.5% in same period
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 50% of instances where RSAFS declined for two consecutive months and CPIAUCSL increased by more than 0.5% in the same period.
